query: Consider the following context: Phonon scattering by SRO precipitates might be expected to reduce scattering times and, therefore, decrease thermal conductivity. In that context, which material can be used for lattice heat conductivity, and why?

generation.hypothesis: A carefully designed thermal treatment that stabilizes or reduces short-range-ordered (SRO) domains in MoNbTaW refractory high-entropy alloys can mitigate phonon scattering and thereby preserve or enhance lattice thermal conductivity.
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast or as-annealed MoNbTaW RHEA containing SRO domains.
generation.intervention: Solutionizing/annealing schedules tuned to reduce or refine SRO domains.
generation.conditions: Moderate to high temperatures relevant to structural or heat-transfer service in refractory alloys.
generation.structural_mediator: Degree, size, and spatial distribution of SRO domains after thermal treatment.
generation.mechanism: Minimizing the extent of SRO domains reduces additional phonon scattering centers, maintaining higher lattice thermal conductivity.
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved or preserved thermal conductivity compared to untreated MoNbTaW with uncontrolled SRO.
generation.baseline: Untreated MoNbTaW RHEA with higher density of larger SRO-rich regions leading to increased phonon scattering.
generation.boundary: Only established for MoNbTaW at certain annealing temperatures; further validations are needed for other refractory HEAs or alternative heat treatments.
generation.uncertainty: Quantitative gains in thermal conductivity remain to be experimentally determined and may vary with specific heat-treatment parameters.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of MoNbTaW samples: one batch with a specific annealing schedule aimed at reducing SRO, and a control batch without targeted SRO refinement. Measure thermal conductivity and microstructure in both sets under identical conditions.
measurements: SRO distribution via X-ray diffraction and TEM
Thermal conductivity using a laser flash apparatus
Microstructure evaluation (grain size, precipitate morphology) by SEM/TEM
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the annealed samples with reduced SRO do not show higher or more stable thermal conductivity compared to the control samples, the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: Refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs) are designed for high elevated-temperature strength, with both edge and screw dislocations playing an important role for plastic deformation. However, they can also display a significant energetic driving force for chemical short-range ordering (SRO). Here, we investigate mechanisms underlying the mobilities of screw and edge dislocations in the body-centered cubic MoNbTaW RHEA over a wide temperature range using extensive molecular dynamics simulations based on a highly-accurate machine-learning interatomic potential. Further, we specifically evaluate how these mechanisms are affected by the presence of SRO. The mobility of edge dislocations is found to be enhanced by the presence of SRO, whereas the rate of double-kink nucleation in the motion of screw dislocations is reduced, although this influence of SRO appears to be attenuated at increasing temperature. Independent of the presence of SRO, a cross-slip locking mechanism is observed for the motion of screws, which provides for extra strengthening for refractory high-entropy alloy system.

Metallic alloys containing multiple principal alloying elements, which are known as high-entropy alloys (HEAs) [1] – [3] , have attracted extensive research interest in recent years with many studies focused on their microstructure, mechanical properties, and underlying deformation mechanisms [4] – [6] . For example, as a new class of structural materials, certain face-centered cubic ( fcc ) alloys, in particular CrCoNi-based HEAs, have been shown to possess improved strength and exceptional damage tolerance, especially at cryogenic temperatures [7] , [8] .

A second prominent class of HEA systems are refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs), which comprise mostly refractory elements and invariably crystallize as body-centered cubic ( bcc ) solid solutions; these alloys have been considered as promising candidate materials for elevated-temperature applications due to their exceptional resistance to softening and extremely high melting points [9] – [11] . decision.trend: Both records from 2021 examine MoNbTaW refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs) in the presence of chemical short-range order (SRO). They show that SRO can significantly alter dislocation mobility and mechanical strengthening but do not address heat conduction directly. No attempts were reported to mitigate phonon-scattering impacts of SRO on thermal conductivity—an open question when such precipitates form in RHEAs and potentially scatter phonons.
decision.unsolved: How to maintain or enhance lattice thermal conductivity in the presence of SRO (or incipient precipitates) without making additional compositional changes remains unexplored.
decision.lever: Implement a carefully designed solutionizing or annealing schedule (e.g., controlling temperature/time profiles) to reduce or stabilize SRO domains and thereby lessen phonon scattering.
decision.why: MoNbTaW RHEAs offer relatively high intrinsic thermal conductivity among refractory alloys. The cited work shows that SRO strongly affects dislocation behavior but leaves open the question of how SRO impacts phonon transport. A targeted thermal treatment to minimize or refine SRO dispersions can preserve the single-phase character needed to sustain higher lattice conductivity, aligning with the question’s aim to mitigate SRO-driven scattering.
